title: Alternating Group
body:
$A_n$: the **even** permutations in the [[Symmetric Group]] $S_n$, meaning those that decompose
into an even number of transpositions. It is a [[Subgroup]] because even composed with even is
even, and it has order

$$|A_n| = \frac{n!}{2} \quad (n \ge 2)$$

so it is exactly half of $S_n$, index 2. The odd permutations are the other [[Coset]] and are not
a subgroup: they miss the identity, and odd composed with odd lands back in $A_n$.

Half is forced rather than lucky. Composing with the fixed transposition $(1\,2)$ is a bijection
between the even and odd halves, so the two are the same size.

$A_3 = \{e, (1\,2\,3), (1\,3\,2)\}$ is cyclic of order 3. $A_4$ has order 12 and is the rotation
group of a tetrahedron. $A_5$, order 60, is the smallest non-abelian **simple** group, and its
simplicity is the reason no formula in radicals solves the general quintic.

Parity itself, the invariant this whole note rests on, is defined in [[Permutation Group]]. It is
the same sign that appears in the permutation expansion of a [[Determinant]].
